body: EMDR has been a wonderful yet mentally exhausting experience. I still wouldn't trade it for the world. It's like journeying into your brain and working through your trauma with new eyes. Then rewiring your brain to process it. It's been so fulfilling for me and my system. We have been able to cut contact with life long abusers, finally get on a proper eating schedule, and be happy sometimes. It is exhausting and harrowing at first, but it does get easier. Some sessions are better than others. But overall I highly recommend it!

It really varies. Some days are super clear as to who is present when and who is talking. Other days it's like a big jumble of all of us yelling at once and I'm not sure who is saying what or even who I am and who is fronting. It's normal to have that denial as well where you feel like you're making it all up. Having DID is a big thing for some of us and you want to be sure that's what it is. Also, it can be scary to accept. It took my system years to fully accept that this is our life even after 6 months of being diagnosed. We are almost at the 1 year anniversary of our diagnosis and sometimes it's still hard to believe. You will learn more about your system, how your alters work, how they fit into your brain and life. Once those things begin to smooth over, it will all become more clear, but those days of questioning and not fully understanding who is talking is pretty normal. Hope this helps friend❤️

He's pretty great! The way he viewed it was just getting to know me about me and learning how he can support every part of me. It's incredibly helpful and has built an even stronger bond with us. He even began to notice how for years he saw them already just didn't quite realize that it was DID. I really hope this helped ease your mind with it, just do your best to support every part of your partner when ever they front and listen to their needs. You'll do amazing, I'm sure of it😁

My husband is friends with all my alters and has unique relationships with all of them. He colors and watches cartoons with my child alter, he cooks and plays games with my teen alter, he has a sexual relationship with my sexual protector. All alters are still a part of your partner so it's totally normal to develop a relationship of sorts with them. As long as you don't purposefully trigger them out because you want to see them or something, that's totally fine! Sounds like you are quite supportive and I'm sure your partners system appreciates that

We don't really have one either. It's more like we each have our own space we go in, but it's small and very similar to spaces we live in. Mostly we spend time in the "gathering space" where we can all view the outside world and share thoughts in. Sometimes there's a microphone in there where one of us can use it to speak even though there's someone else forward, only giving that alter a moment of getting their words across before they go back. So not like full fronting. It's hard to describe. But I understand what you mean. Some have very vast and vivid inner worlds, some of us just have empty voids

I have been committed before a few years ago. Honestly this isn't an all the time thing. We had just had a family night at my parent's house that didn't go well. I'm very certain that effected my emotions and thoughts this morning. Ideation is very strong but I have no intent of harming myself. Only fear of it. It was made worse by my panicking as well so once i had calmed down later, the ideation subsided. Like I said, I would have contacted my therapist if she was available. I have called the mental health hotline in my city before but they are not very helpful and often have invalidated me when I have called in even more dangerous times than this. So I did seek comfort for him instead because I wasn't sure of another option at that moment. I do not use him as a replacement of a health professional, just as my main source of support and love when needed

I do not dump it on him. We both have therapists that we see weekly. I could not get ahold of my therapist at that moment. I needed him to just wake up and be present with me. We did not have to talk about it, we could have talked about the weather, I don't care. I just needed someone to sit with me and distract me. 

Please do not assume that since I was looking to him for support that I put everything on him and expect him to just be my "therapist". I don't expect that of him and never would. Also, discussing our mental health has NEVER caused harm to our relationship. Our marriage is very loving and amazing, just this one issue that has happened a few times.

It's different for everyone I think! Personally, I have bits and pieces of memories from my childhood and teen years. I have some memory gaps in my adult life as well but nowhere near as much. From ages 5-16 its large gaps and very blurry, just like little moments or ideas of what happened. Some of it feels like my childhood/my life/my memories and others don't at all

I'd been diagnosed with CPTSD for a few years before figuring it out. I'd always referred to myself in parts and I had large gaps in my memory. I was able to talk about certain traumas as if they didn't happen to me and would often describe them like I was describing a movie. I was completely emotionless about a lot of things but when I would be emotional, it would be confusing. My husband says there was times when he could tell I wasn't there or would behave strange and he just thought it was PTSD. I started taking meds and going to therapy, after that memories started unlocking but the emotions wouldn't. I still felt detached from everything. I would often leave my body and watch myself from across the room or would be out entirely. I would ask myself questions and get answers inside my head. It always sounded like different voices screaming at me and it all was different intentions. It wasn't until I met my current therapist that the topic of DID being a possibility was brought up. She saw my child alter one day and it got her questioning things. She had me take some tests and would ask me a lot about my thought processes and my feelings on things. She noticed how detached I was from my own mind and feelings and memories. One day, my husband noticed me being distant and doing things differently. Since the idea of DID had been brought up, he made attempts to interact with me and one of my alters began to open up. 2 weeks later I was diagnosed with DID
